# Project overview

This PIPS group project will investigate how selective publication changes
meta-analytic effect estimates in simulated psychological experiments.

The Mozart effect debate motivates the project. However, our simulation will
not establish whether publication bias caused the historical Mozart effect.

# Research question

How do publication-selection mechanisms influence estimated psychological
effects, and how reliably can selected statistical methods identify the
resulting distortions?

# Planned workflow

1. Generate participant-level data for simulated psychological experiments.
2. Calculate study-level effect estimates and sampling variances.
3. Apply a clearly specified publication filter.
4. Compare meta-analyses of all studies and published studies.
5. Evaluate estimates and selected bias-detection methods across repeated
   simulations.
6. Present informative figures and discuss limitations.

The team will agree on the exact simulation settings, effect-size measure,
and statistical methods before integrating these modules.

# Development status

This initial document contains the project overview and an R environment
record. The simulation, publication filter, statistical analyses, and figures
are not implemented in this version. It is not yet a complete course
submission and does not report scientific results.

Supporting functions will be stored in `src/` and called from this document
as the team completes and reviews them.
